A private static helper that compares the scheme, host and port of two URLs. It supports the grant URL test, but is a trivial implementation detail called only by TestGrantUrl and has no architectural standing of its own.

Integration event handler subscribing to OrderPaymentSucceeded from the event bus. It translates the event into a SetPaidOrderStatusCommand and dispatches it via the mediator. This is an event-triggered application function. It consumes cross-service messages and logs handling, which is incidental observability.

A simple enumeration of webhook event types (price change, shipped, paid) in the WebhookClient. Enumerations are modelled as schemadefinitions in the data-model layer. It is a small domain type with no callers shown, so its significance is low.

This is a single method declaration on the client app's IOrderService interface. The interface as a whole could be modelled as an application service or interface, but one abstract method signature is below the granularity of an architecture element. It contains no implementation, so it carries none of the concerns itself.

Interface contract for the ordering service's idempotency request manager, which checks for and records processed command request IDs in durable storage. It is a notable infrastructure component abstraction behind idempotent command handling, not a trivial helper. The contract itself defines the persistence role that its implementation fulfils.

A trivial XAML value converter that multiplies an item count by a fixed height for layout binding. It is a UI formatting helper below the granularity of an architectural element and has no callers or architectural responsibility of its own.

Auto-generated EF Core migration designer snapshot. It is generated boilerplate that duplicates the target model for tooling. The migration itself and the tables it creates are the data-store evidence; this designer file is not an architectural element on its own.

Trivial IDisposable boilerplate that removes a change subscription from the owning BasketState's list. It is an implementation detail of the subscription mechanism and not an architectural element. The listed callers are spurious name-based matches from test fixtures.

WebApp composition root: wires DI for application services, the RabbitMQ event bus subscriptions, gRPC and HTTP clients to the basket, catalog and ordering APIs, AI chat clients, and OIDC/cookie authentication. It is a central bootstrap module, so it is modelled as an application component; it configures authentication directly and integrates with external services.

This is an EF Core-generated migration Designer partial class that snapshots the target model for the migration. It is generated boilerplate, not an architectural element itself. The migration and the tables it describes would be modelled elsewhere in the data-store layer.

BadgeView is a reusable MAUI UI control. It declares bindable properties (Text, TextColor, BadgeColor, FontSize) and a Content slot, and is not a routable screen. That makes it a library component in the UX layer. It is a notable but minor widget in the client app.

An MVC HTTP GET action (Account/AccessDenied) that only returns the access-denied view. It is a distinct method-path endpoint, so it fits api operation, but it is trivial IdentityServer quickstart boilerplate with no logic. It renders a page, so user_interface applies; it makes no authorization decision itself.

Small extension-method helper that reads the authenticated user's 'sub' claim from the authentication state to derive the buyer ID. It touches identity, so authentication is flagged, but it is a trivial accessor below the modelling granularity, not an authentication mechanism or a security element in its own right.

This is a passive view-model record that carries the two-factor verification form input (provider, code, return URL, remember flags). It only holds data passed between the view and the account controller. It has no behaviour of its own and is not persisted or published as a schema, so it is a minor application DataObject. [Revised 2026-11-17, gold-revise.ts 'declared-shape': a class that only declares fields is a data-model object schema; a data object is a class with logic of its own over its state.]

EF Core migration that creates the IntegrationEventLog outbox table for the Catalog database. It is the physical definition of a persisted collection used by the transactional outbox pattern, which makes it architecturally significant persistence structure in the data-store layer.

A one-line computed accessor on the Order aggregate that sums the order items' units multiplied by unit price. It is a domain helper below modelling granularity; the Order aggregate itself would be the element. It performs no persistence, I/O or other cross-cutting work.

Trivial constructor that only assigns OrderId and OrderItems. The architecturally meaningful element is the enclosing OrderStatusChangedToPaidDomainEvent class, an application event. The constructor itself is boilerplate and not an element in its own right.

A trivial XAML value converter that extracts the URL string from WebNavigatingEventArgs for data binding. It is MVVM UI plumbing and a formatting helper with no architectural identity of its own, so it sits below the granularity of any modelled element.

MVVM view model backing the profile screen in the MAUI client. It loads the user's orders through the order service and drives navigation to logout and order detail. It is a presentation-logic component, not the view itself, so it sits in the application layer. It drives the UI, but logout is only a navigation call and performs no authentication itself.

This is a MAUI XAML page code-behind for the catalog item screen. It binds its view model and initializes the UI, so it is a top-level UI surface in the client app and is modelled as a UX view. Its code-behind is trivial, but the screen itself is architecturally nameable.

A view model for IdentityServer's device-authorization consent page, taken from the Quickstart UI scaffolding. It is a two-property DTO extending ConsentViewModel with no behaviour and no callers. It is a sample implementation detail rather than a named architectural element, so it is not modelled and has low significance.

Entry point/bootstrap of the PaymentProcessor microservice: wires RabbitMQ event bus subscription for stock-confirmed integration events, binds options, and runs the host. Represents the deployable PaymentProcessor application component and its integration with the message broker.

Declares the IdentityServer API scopes (orders, basket, webhooks), which are access entitlements granted to clients and checked by APIs. That makes it authorization configuration in the security layer, closest to permission grants. It is a static config method used at startup, so it is notable but not core.

A plain C# record in the web app components that carries catalog item data received from the catalog API to UI components. It is not a persisted entity or a published schema, so it is an application data object that the web front end passes between its parts. [Revised 2026-11-17, gold-revise.ts 'declared-shape': a class that only declares fields is a data-model object schema; a data object is a class with logic of its own over its state.]

Domain aggregate-root behaviour enforcing the order-item invariants (merging lines and applying higher discounts). It is a notable unit of internal business logic invoked by command handlers, not a contract or a persistence call, so it is modelled as an application function. It only mutates in-memory state.

A DI service contract in the eShop MAUI client that exposes app configuration (endpoints, mock flags, location) and user-token get/set. As an interface it is the access point to the settings service. It holds no implementation, so no concern is implemented here. It is a notable internal unit.

An empty partial class that exists only to trigger System.Text.Json source generation for CustomerBasket serialization in the Redis repository. It is generated-code scaffolding and an implementation detail, not an architectural element. It performs no persistence itself.

An HTTP GET controller action (External/Callback) on the identity service that completes external-provider authentication. It reads the external cookie, provisions the user, issues the local session cookie and redirects. It is a method+path contract and an authentication boundary, so it is modelled as an API operation.

Interface in the eShop MAUI client that aggregates the basket, catalog, order and identity service contracts and lets the app switch between mock and real implementations. It is an access-point contract for a service locator, a notable but internal composition unit. It does not perform the cross-cutting work itself.

Source-generated LoggerMessage definition declaring a structured log event (EventId 3, named template, Trace level) emitted by a domain event handler. It defines a kind of log record, so it belongs to apm as a LogRecord. It is a minor, single-caller telemetry definition, hence low significance.

EF Core migration that moves the orderitemseq sequence into the ordering schema and drops column defaults on two tables. Migrations are data-store evidence, but this is a small, largely generated schema fix. No migration element type exists, so element_type is null and significance is low.

A MediatR command handler in the eShop Ordering service. It reacts to a stock-rejected command by loading the order, cancelling it and saving through the repository. It is an internal application function triggered by a command. Persistence is delegated to the repository, so the symbol itself does not implement data_persistence.

Interface method declaration on the client app's IBasketService contract: one operation of the basket application service. It is minor on its own, since the service interface is the modelled element. It is declaration only, so no concern is implemented here.

A small enum in the MAUI client that lists device OS permission kinds (location variants). It is not user access-control logic or a domain data schema. It is a trivial supporting type below the granularity of an architecture element.

Integration event published via the event bus when an order becomes paid, triggering other services such as Catalog stock updates. It represents a cross-service state-change occurrence, so it is an applicationevent. As a contract between microservices it is architecturally significant.

An in-memory pub/sub service in the eShop WebApp. It manages per-buyer subscriptions and notifies subscribers when an order's status changes, so the UI can refresh. It is a cohesive, DI-registered class with its own responsibility, making it an application component of moderate significance. No persistence or external calls.

Constructor of DeviceController that only assigns injected dependencies to fields. It is dependency-injection boilerplate with no behaviour of its own. The controller class may be architecturally relevant, but this constructor is not an element by itself.

BasketItem is a plain property-only record inside the WebApp services, used by BasketState to carry basket line data. It is not persisted as an entity or published as a schema, so it is an application data object. It is a minor unit relevant only to its module. [Revised 2026-11-17, gold-revise.ts 'declared-shape': a class that only declares fields is a data-model object schema; a data object is a class with logic of its own over its state.]

Client-side DTO that deserializes OIDC userinfo claims (sub, preferred_username, email) in the eShop mobile client. It is a passive data carrier with no behaviour and is neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application DataObject. It is notable because it holds identity and payment profile data.

This is the generated-style XAML code-behind for BasketItemTemplate. Its only content is a constructor calling InitializeComponent(), which is boilerplate. The meaningful UX element, the basket item template, lives in the XAML markup. This code-behind module adds no architectural content of its own.

Protoc-generated serialization method on a gRPC message class (GeneratedCode attribute). It is boilerplate wire-format plumbing, below the granularity of an architecture element; the message type itself, not its WriteTo method, would be modelled if anything.

This is the standard .NET MAUI Android platform bootstrap class. It only forwards the JNI handle to its base class and delegates to MauiProgram.CreateMauiApp. It is generated-style boilerplate with no logic of its own. The meaningful entry point is MauiProgram, not this platform shim.

An integration event record that the ordering service publishes over the event bus and the Catalog API consumes to trigger stock validation. It represents a named state-change occurrence exchanged between services, so it is an ApplicationEvent and a cross-service integration point.

A single method declaration on the ILoginService interface, with no body and no callers. It is part of the login contract rather than an element in its own right; the ILoginService interface would be the modelled unit. It does declare a sign-in (authentication) operation.

EF Core entity class (Required/NotMapped attributes) persisted in the integration event log table for the transactional outbox pattern. Under the charter, an ORM-mapped entity is a data-model object schema. It is a central contract of the outbox mechanism, though it performs no I/O itself.

Domain event handler body reacting to OrderStartedDomainEvent: validates or creates the Buyer aggregate, verifies the payment method, persists via the unit of work and enqueues an integration event. It is an application function triggered by an event. Logging is delegated to a trace helper, so observability is not set.

CatalogType is an EF Core entity class in eShop's Catalog API model, with an Id and a required Type field. A persisted entity is an object schema in the data-model layer. It is a small supporting entity that classifies catalog items, so significance is 2.

Abstract base for a MAUI/Xamarin UI animation. It defines reusable motion parameters: duration, easing, delay and repeat. This matches a transition template, but it is a framework-level base class with minor architectural significance.

Constructor of a MAUI/Xamarin ContentPage base class that only blanks the navigation back-button title. It is trivial UI boilerplate below modelling granularity; the base page class, not this constructor, would be the element. It does touch UI presentation.

Event handler that consumes the OrderPaymentSucceeded integration event from the event bus and dispatches a SetPaidOrderStatusCommand via the mediator. As an event-triggered handler of a single component, it is an application function. Its logging is incidental, and it serves as a cross-service integration consumer.

Trivial override returning a constant true to ignore duplicate requests in an idempotent command handler. It is an implementation detail of the identified-command pattern, not an architectural element on its own.

A trivial configuration helper extension method that reads a required config value or throws. It is a utility below the granularity of an architecture element and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Generic EF Core-backed service implementing the transactional outbox. It saves integration events within the caller's DB transaction, retrieves pending ones and updates their publish state. It is a reusable, dependency-injected component shared across services, so it is architecturally significant. It persists data directly through DbContext, but it does not publish events or call external systems itself.

Adds a received webhook to an in-memory queue and notifies change subscribers. It is the core write operation of the HooksRepository component, called from the webhook endpoint. Storage is in-memory only, not durable, so no persistence concern applies. It is an internal application function rather than an API contract.

ChatState is the AI chatbot concierge component. It holds the conversation state, calls an external LLM chat client, and exposes tools for catalog search and basket actions. Its injected collaborators and business logic make it an application component; it integrates with an external AI service and logs errors.

An alternative IOrderService implementation that returns canned in-memory orders. MauiProgram registers it in DI for the app's mock mode, and unit tests also reuse it. It is a replaceable application component, notable but secondary to the real order service. It does no storage, integration or UI work itself.

An event handler, triggered by the OrderStatusChangedToAwaitingValidation integration event, that validates stock against the catalog DB and publishes confirmed or rejected events. It is a key cross-service integration point in the ordering saga, modelled as an application function. It reads the DbContext directly, and its logging is incidental.

Constructor of IdentityService that only assigns injected dependencies to fields. It is dependency-injection boilerplate with no behaviour of its own. The IdentityService class may be architecturally significant, but this constructor is not an element and implements no concern itself.

MAUI XAML page code-behind for the Profile screen. It binds the ProfileViewModel and refreshes data on appearing. It is a top-level UI surface, so it maps to ux.view. Its significance is moderate as one screen in the client app.

Auto-generated gRPC client stub (protoc grpc_csharp_plugin, 'DO NOT EDIT'). It is generated boilerplate. The architectural fact is the Basket gRPC service contract and the client integration that uses it, not this generated file. It does perform remote calls to the Basket API, so it touches external integration.

A trivial constructor that only assigns UserId on the OrderStartedIntegrationEvent class. The event class itself would be modelled as an application event, but this constructor is boilerplate and an implementation detail with no architectural meaning of its own.

A MediatR command record that only carries an order number to a handler that marks the order as paid. It holds state and has no behaviour, so it is an application data object. It names a notable step in the ordering workflow but is not a service or contract.

This is the code-behind for a XAML item template that renders one basket line item. The C# body is only InitializeComponent boilerplate, but the partial class stands for a reusable UI template. It is modelled as a minor UX library component with low significance.
